scenario: 系统设计面追问并发:两个后台任务各拿了一把锁,又都在等对方那把,整个流程卡死。面试官问怎么回事、怎么修。她想说这是死锁、靠统一加锁顺序解决,却卡在词上。
scenario_en: A concurrency follow-up: two background tasks each hold one lock and wait on the other, so everything hangs. She wants to say it's a deadlock fixed by a consistent lock ordering, but stalls on the term.
q: 想说「这是死锁——两个线程各拿一把锁又互等,我们靠统一加锁顺序解决」,该怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you say 'it's a deadlock — each thread holds one lock and waits on the other, so we impose a lock ordering'?
options: It's a dead-lock, the two threads lock each other, so we give them a lock order to not lock.
It's a deadlock — each thread holds one lock and waits on the other. We fixed it by always acquiring the locks in the same order.
So so the two threads, they they each hold a lock and, and wait for the other one, and it just, it just hangs.
A deadlock manifests when threads acquire locks in incompatible orders; enforcing a canonical global acquisition order eliminates the cyclic wait.
tradeoff: 地道 deadlock + lock ordering vs 卡壳:前者一句点出环等和修法;'they lock each other' 听不出你懂机制。
why: 术语是 deadlock:各持一锁、互相等待成环;修法说 acquire the locks in the same order,点出统一顺序才算懂机制。
why_en: Name the deadlock — each thread holds one lock and waits on the other — then fix it by acquiring the locks in one consistent order.
whenOtherWins: 如果全程只有一把锁,就没有死锁问题,直接说 'a single lock, no ordering needed' 即可。
options_en: It's a dead-lock, the two threads lock each other, so we give them a lock order to not lock.
It's a deadlock — each thread holds one lock and waits on the other. We fixed it by always acquiring the locks in the same order.
So so the two threads, they they each hold a lock and, and wait for the other one, and it just, it just hangs.
A deadlock manifests when threads acquire locks in incompatible orders; enforcing a canonical global acquisition order eliminates the cyclic wait.

地道:死锁+各持一锁互等+统一加锁顺序。
反复 they、wait,绕在描述里落不到词。
教科书腔:念 cyclic wait、canonical order。
optionMeanings_en: Chinglish 'dead-lock, lock each other'; wrong form, vague mechanism.
Idiomatic: deadlock plus hold-and-wait plus a consistent lock ordering.
Loops on 'they they, wait for', never lands the term.
Textbook: 'cyclic wait, canonical order', sounds read aloud.
optionScenarioImpacts: 听不出你懂环等,像只会描述现象。
一句点出死锁和修法,显得你真修过。

太书面像背的,显不出实际调过并发。

One line names the deadlock and the fix; they see you've fixed one.
They wait for the term while you circle; you lose the floor.
Too bookish, sounds memorized; hides real concurrency work.

抓住互等到统一顺序的因果。
错在时机:当场绕圈出不来。
错在语域:口语别念 cyclic/canonical。

Nails the hold-and-wait to lock-ordering chain.

Wrong register: no 'cyclic/canonical' when speaking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 死锁:两个或多个线程各自持有对方需要的锁,谁都不肯放手,于是永远互相等待、谁也走不下去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock is when two or more threads each hold a lock the other needs and neither releases, so both wait forever.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加锁顺序:规定所有线程都按同一个固定顺序去获取多把锁,从而打破环形等待、避免死锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock ordering means all threads acquire multiple locks in the same fixed order, which breaks the cycle and prevents deadlock.

scenario: 并发追问:一个计数器被多线程更新,面试官不想用锁,问怎么无锁地安全更新。她想说用 CAS——读旧值、只在没被改过时写入、否则重试,却说不利落。
scenario_en: A concurrency follow-up: a counter is updated by many threads and the interviewer wants no lock — how do you update it safely? She wants to say CAS: read, swap in only if unchanged, else retry, but it comes out clumsy.
q: 想说「用 compare-and-swap 无锁更新——只在值没变时写入,变了就重试」,怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say 'a compare-and-swap for a lock-free update — write only if the value hasn't changed, retry if it has'?
options: We use a compare-swap, we compare the value and change it without lock.
So so instead of a lock we we read it and then, then write it back, and if if someone changed it we try again.
We use a compare-and-swap — read the value, swap the new one in only if it hasn't changed, and retry if it has.
The update employs an atomic compare-and-swap primitive that commits only when the observed value matches the expected value, retrying under contention.
tradeoff: 地道 CAS + 条件重试 vs 卡壳:前者点出无锁机制;'compare-swap, change without lock' 听不出你懂重试。
why: 术语是 CAS(compare-and-swap):只在值没被改过时写入、否则重试——点出这个条件重试才算懂无锁。
why_en: Say compare-and-swap — write only if the value is unchanged, and retry on failure; the retry loop is what proves it's lock-free.
whenOtherWins: 如果争用很高、重试太多,退回锁或原子指令更稳,可说 'under heavy contention we'd just lock'。
options_en: We use a compare-swap, we compare the value and change it without lock.
So so instead of a lock we we read it and then, then write it back, and if if someone changed it we try again.
We use a compare-and-swap — read the value, swap the new one in only if it hasn't changed, and retry if it has.
The update employs an atomic compare-and-swap primitive that commits only when the observed value matches the expected value, retrying under contention.

反复 we we、try again,绕着说没落到词。
地道:CAS+只在没变时写入+失败重试。
教科书腔:念 primitive、observed value。
optionMeanings_en: Chinglish 'compare-swap'; wrong form and drops the retry.
Loops on 'we we, try again', never lands the term.
Idiomatic: CAS plus write-only-if-unchanged plus retry.

对方等 CAS 那个词,你却一直绕。

太书面像背的,显不出你写过无锁。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They can't tell you grasp the retry; sounds vague.
They wait for 'CAS' while you circle the description.
One line names lock-free and the retry; they nod.
Too bookish; hides that you've written lock-free code.

错在时机:当场绕圈丢主动。
抓住条件写到重试的因果。
错在语域:口语别念 primitive。

termDefinitions.meaning: 比较并交换(CAS):一条原子指令,先检查内存里的值是否等于预期值,相等才写入新值,不等就失败、由调用方重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-swap (CAS) atomically checks whether a value equals the expected one and writes the new value only if it does, else it fails and you retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无锁:多个线程不用互斥锁也能安全更新共享数据,通常靠 CAS 这类原子指令加失败重试来实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock-free means threads update shared data safely without a mutex, typically via atomic ops like CAS plus a retry on failure.

scenario: 并发追问:服务会瞬间开几百个线程去调下游,把下游打挂。面试官问怎么限制同时并发数。她想说用信号量把并发上限卡在 N,却卡词。
scenario_en: A concurrency follow-up: the service spawns hundreds of threads hitting a downstream and overwhelms it. How do you cap concurrent access? She wants to say a semaphore caps it at N, but stalls.
q: 想说「用一个带 N 个许可的信号量,最多只放 N 个线程同时进」,怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say 'a semaphore with N permits, so at most N threads run concurrently'?
options: We put a semaphore with ten permits in front of it, so at most ten threads hit the downstream at once.
We use a semaphore counter to limit how many thread can go in at the same time.
So so we we want to hold them back, so not too many, not too many threads go in at, at once, you know.
A counting semaphore initialized to ten bounds the number of threads permitted to enter the critical section concurrently.
tradeoff: 地道 semaphore + N permits vs 卡壳:前者点出许可上限;'semaphore counter to limit' 听不出你懂机制。
why: 术语是 semaphore:点出「N 个 permits、最多 N 个同时进」——许可数量才证明你懂它怎么限并发。
why_en: Say a semaphore with N permits, so at most N threads enter at once; naming the permit count proves you know how it caps concurrency.
whenOtherWins: 如果要跨进程、跨机器限流,单机信号量不够,得用分布式限流,可说 'a distributed rate limiter instead'。
options_en: We put a semaphore with ten permits in front of it, so at most ten threads hit the downstream at once.
We use a semaphore counter to limit how many thread can go in at the same time.
So so we we want to hold them back, so not too many, not too many threads go in at, at once, you know.
A counting semaphore initialized to ten bounds the number of threads permitted to enter the critical section concurrently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 信号量:一个带固定数量许可(permit)的计数器,线程进来先拿一个许可、出去再还,许可用完的线程就得排队等待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A semaphore is a counter with a fixed number of permits; a thread takes one to enter and returns it on exit, and when permits run out, others wait.

termDefinitions.meaning: 许可:信号量里可被占用的名额;有 N 个许可就意味着最多允许 N 个线程同时进入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A permit is a slot in the semaphore; N permits means at most N threads may be inside at the same time.

scenario: 并发追问:线程池该开多大?面试官想听你怎么权衡。她想说太少会让请求排队饿死、太多会在上下文切换上抖动,却憋不出 thrash 这个词。
scenario_en: A concurrency follow-up: how big should the thread pool be? The interviewer wants your tradeoff. She wants to say too few threads starve requests and too many thrash on context switches, but can't get 'thrash' out.
q: 想说「按负载定线程池大小——太少请求会饿死,太多会在上下文切换上抖动」,怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say 'size the pool to the workload — too few starve, too many thrash on context switches'?
options: We set the thread pool size, if too small the thread is not enough, if too big the CPU is busy switching.
So so the number of threads, if it's, if it's too low then things wait, and too high then it, it gets slow somehow.
The thread pool must be sized to the workload; insufficient parallelism starves throughput whereas excessive parallelism induces context-switch overhead.
We size the pool to the workload — too few threads and requests starve, too many and they thrash on context switches.
tradeoff: 地道 starve vs thrash 两端 vs 卡壳:前者一句点出双向代价;'CPU is busy switching' 听不出你懂权衡。
why: 术语是 size the pool、thrash:一句带出两端——too few starve、too many thrash,点出双向代价才算懂。
why_en: Say you size the pool to the workload — too few threads starve throughput, too many thrash on context switches; naming both ends shows the tradeoff.
whenOtherWins: 如果是纯 IO 等待的任务,线程多点也不太 thrash,可说 'for IO-bound work you can oversize a bit'。
options_en: We set the thread pool size, if too small the thread is not enough, if too big the CPU is busy switching.
So so the number of threads, if it's, if it's too low then things wait, and too high then it, it gets slow somehow.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抖动/颠簸:线程太多时,CPU 大部分时间花在线程间来回切换上下文上,真正干活的时间反而变少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thrashing is when there are so many threads that the CPU spends most of its time switching between them instead of doing real work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 饿死:线程太少时,请求排队却拿不到线程执行,吞吐被压低、延迟升高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Starvation here is when there are too few threads, so requests queue up and can't get one to run on, dragging throughput down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上下文切换:CPU 从一个线程切到另一个时保存旧状态、恢复新状态的开销,线程越多切换越频繁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A context switch is the CPU's cost of saving one thread's state and restoring another's; more threads means more frequent switches.

scenario: 并发追问:一份配置读得非常多、偶尔才写一次,用普通互斥锁连读都要排队。面试官问怎么优化。她想说用读写锁——多个读并行、写独占,却说成 'read pass' 之类。
scenario_en: A concurrency follow-up: a config is read constantly but written rarely, and a plain mutex serializes even reads. How do you optimize? She wants to say a read-write lock — many readers in parallel, one exclusive writer — but garbles the term.
q: 想说「用读写锁——任意多个读可以同时拿,写的时候独占」,怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say 'a read-write lock — many readers together, but a writer takes it exclusively'?
options: We use a read-write lock, many read can go together and the write must be alone.
We use a read-write lock — any number of readers can hold it together, but a writer takes it exclusively.
So so it's a lock but for for reads it's shared, and then for, for writes only one, only one can go.
A read-write lock permits concurrent shared acquisition by multiple readers while mandating exclusive acquisition for any writer.
tradeoff: 地道 shared readers vs exclusive writer vs 卡壳:前者点出并行读;'read pass, many read' 听不出你懂机制。
why: 术语是 read-write lock:点出「多读共享、写独占」——这对区分才证明你懂读多写少为何更快。
why_en: Say a read-write lock — readers share it, a writer takes it exclusively; that shared-vs-exclusive contrast proves you get why it helps read-heavy loads.
whenOtherWins: 如果读写差不多多,读写锁的额外开销可能不值,普通 mutex 更简单,可说 'a plain mutex is simpler here'。
options_en: We use a read-write lock, many read can go together and the write must be alone.
We use a read-write lock — any number of readers can hold it together, but a writer takes it exclusively.
So so it's a lock but for for reads it's shared, and then for, for writes only one, only one can go.
A read-write lock permits concurrent shared acquisition by multiple readers while mandating exclusive acquisition for any writer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读写锁:允许多个读线程同时持有(共享锁),但写线程必须独占(排他锁),适合读远多于写的场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read-write lock lets many readers hold it at once (shared mode) but requires a writer to hold it alone (exclusive mode), ideal for read-heavy loads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 独占/排他:写线程拿锁时,其它任何读或写线程都必须等待,保证写的时候没人在读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exclusive means that while a writer holds the lock, every other reader and writer must wait, so nobody reads mid-write.

scenario: 并发追问:一个全局计数只是加一,面试官问有没有比加锁更轻的办法。她想说直接用原子计数器——自增是单条原子操作、不用锁,却说成 'atomic operation to plus one'。
scenario_en: A concurrency follow-up: a global counter just increments, and the interviewer asks for something lighter than a lock. She wants to say use an atomic counter — the increment is one atomic op, no lock — but says 'atomic operation to plus one.'
q: 想说「别加锁,直接用原子计数器——自增是单条原子操作,线程之间没法交错」,怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say 'skip the lock, use an atomic counter — the increment is a single atomic op'?
options: We use an atomic counter to plus one, no need lock because it is atomic operation.
So so instead of a lock we we just add to it, and it's, it's safe because it's atomic, atomic somehow.
We drop the lock and use an atomic counter — the increment is a single atomic op, so threads can't interleave.
Rather than guarding the counter with a mutex, we utilize an atomic fetch-and-add instruction that guarantees indivisible increments.
tradeoff: 地道 atomic increment + 不可交错 vs 卡壳:前者点出无锁;'atomic operation to plus one' 听不出你懂机制。
why: 术语是 atomic counter:点出「自增是单条原子操作、无法被交错」——这才证明你懂它为何不用锁。
why_en: Say an atomic counter — the increment is a single atomic op that can't be interleaved, so no lock is needed; that's what proves you get it.
whenOtherWins: 如果要同时改好几个变量、还得保持一致,单个原子操作不够,得回到锁,可说 'multiple fields need a lock'。

We drop the lock and use an atomic counter — the increment is a single atomic op, so threads can't interleave.
Rather than guarding the counter with a mutex, we utilize an atomic fetch-and-add instruction that guarantees indivisible increments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子计数器:对计数的自增或自减是不可分割的单条硬件操作,多线程并发也不会互相干扰,因此无需加锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic counter's increment or decrement is a single indivisible hardware op, so concurrent threads don't corrupt it and no lock is needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 交错:两个线程的操作步骤穿插着执行;原子操作能保证中间不会被别的线程插进来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To interleave is for two threads' steps to run intermixed; an atomic op guarantees no other thread slips in partway through.

termDefinitions.meaning: 取值并加:一条原子指令,读出当前值的同时把它加上给定量,常用来实现无锁自增。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fetch-and-add is one atomic instruction that reads the current value and adds to it in the same step, often used for lock-free increments.

scenario: 并发追问:一堆共享状态被多线程改得很乱、锁也满天飞。面试官问有没有干脆不用锁的设计。她想说把状态限制在单线程、让一个 actor 独占它、全走消息,却卡词。
scenario_en: A concurrency follow-up: shared state is mutated by many threads and locks are everywhere. Is there a design that avoids locks entirely? She wants to say confine the state to one thread — an actor owns it, everything goes through messages — but stalls.
q: 想说「把状态限制在单线程——一个 actor 独占它,改动都走消息,就没有共享可变状态要锁」,怎么说?
q_en: How do you say 'confine the state to one thread — an actor owns it, so there's no shared mutable state to lock'?
options: We confine the state to one thread — an actor owns it, all changes go through its mailbox, so there's no shared state to lock.
We use actor model, the actor keep the state itself, so other thread cannot touch it and no need lock.
So so only one, only one thread owns the state, and others just, just send messages, so we we don't lock.
State mutation is confined to a single thread of control; the owning actor serializes all access through message passing, thereby obviating locks entirely.
tradeoff: 地道 confine + 无共享所以无锁 vs 卡壳:前者点出因果;'actor keep the state itself' 听不出你懂为何免锁。
why: 术语是 thread confinement:点出「一个 actor 独占状态、无共享可变状态、所以不用锁」——这个因果才算懂。
why_en: Say you confine the state to one thread — an actor owns it, so there's no shared mutable state and no lock; that no-sharing-so-no-lock chain is the point.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态天然要被多方并行读写、又不能串行化,actor 的单点就成瓶颈,可说 'the single owner becomes a bottleneck'。
options_en: We confine the state to one thread — an actor owns it, all changes go through its mailbox, so there's no shared state to lock.
We use actor model, the actor keep the state itself, so other thread cannot touch it and no need lock.
So so only one, only one thread owns the state, and others just, just send messages, so we we don't lock.
State mutation is confined to a single thread of control; the owning actor serializes all access through message passing, thereby obviating locks entirely.
optionMeanings: 地道:状态限单线程+actor 独占+走消息+免锁。
词形错:keep the state itself,漏了免锁因果。
反复 only one、we we,绕着说没落词。
教科书腔:念 confined、obviating。
optionMeanings_en: Idiomatic: confine to one thread plus actor owns plus messages plus no lock.
Chinglish 'keep the state itself'; drops the no-lock logic.
Loops on 'only one, we we', never lands the term.
Textbook: 'confined, obviating', reads off a page.

听不出你懂为何免锁,像只套了词。
对方等那个因果,你却含糊带过。
太书面像背的,显不出实践。

They can't tell why it avoids locks; sounds like buzzwords.

错在词形,免锁因果没点透。
错在时机:当场绕圈出不来。
错在语域:口语别念 obviating。

Wrong form; the no-lock logic never lands.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线程封闭:把某份状态限制在单个线程里访问,别的线程碰不到,因此天然没有并发冲突、不需要加锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thread confinement keeps a piece of state accessible from only one thread, so no other thread can touch it and no lock is required.

termDefinitions.meaning: actor:一个独占自己私有状态的并发单元,外界只能给它发消息、由它自己串行处理,从而避免共享可变状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An actor is a concurrency unit that owns its private state; others only send it messages, which it processes one at a time, so state is never shared.

termDefinitions.meaning: 邮箱:actor 的消息队列;所有发给它的请求先进邮箱排队,再被它逐条处理,保证一次只处理一条。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mailbox is an actor's message queue; requests to it queue up there and it handles them one by one, so only one is processed at a time.
